title: Monitoring and Auto Scaling
description: Use logs, metrics, and alarms to keep an eye on your ASP.NET Core app running on Elastic Beanstalk.

data.text: Elastic Beanstalk provides built-in logging, metrics, and health monitoring. For deeper telemetry, CloudWatch Alarms and dashboards give you operational visibility.

data.title: Enable log streaming to CloudWatch
data.content:
Configure Elastic Beanstalk to stream logs to CloudWatch Logs.
# Expected output: Configuration settings are updated successfully.

items: Elastic Beanstalk health dashboard shows instance health, CPU, and network
CloudWatch Metrics include CPUUtilization, NetworkIn, and request counts
Health monitoring can trigger Auto Scaling policies

data.text: Auto Scaling keeps a minimum number of instances running and adds more when CPU or request count exceeds a threshold.

data.title: Configure Auto Scaling triggers
data.content:
Use the AWS CLI to create scaling triggers based on CPU utilization.
# Expected output: Auto Scaling triggers are configured.

data.title: Add health checks and observe metrics
data.description: Enable health checks in ASP.NET Core and observe them in Elastic Beanstalk.
steps: Browse the app and trigger an error
View logs and metrics in the Elastic Beanstalk console
data.expectedOutcome: You see request logs and health status in the Elastic Beanstalk console.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Elastic Beanstalk provides built-in health dashboards and log access
CloudWatch Logs centralize application and platform logs
Auto Scaling maintains availability under load
Health checks give Elastic Beanstalk a simple readiness signal
data.takeaway: Elastic Beanstalk diagnostics integrate cleanly with ASP.NET Core health checks for production readiness.
